pick.name: TypeScript + React everywhere: Next.js (web) + Expo (Android/iOS) + Electron (desktop) + Hono API + Drizzle, in a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo
pick.what: apps/web, apps/mobile, apps/desktop, apps/api share packages/{schema (zod), api-client, db (Drizzle), domain logic, auth client, tokens}
pick.why: One language and one React mental model across all 3 clients + API; the stack Claude Code writes best; every piece has the largest ecosystem in its category
pick.free_limits: all OSS; costs only come from hosting/stores
pick.install: npx create-better-t-stack@latest (see starter slot) or pnpm dlx create-turbo@latest

alts.name: Expo-universal (Expo Router for iOS/Android/web, Electron wraps the Expo web build)
alts.what: One React Native UI codebase rendered on web via react-native-web
alts.why: Highest UI reuse (~80-90%) for app-like products with little SEO need

alts.name: Flutter everywhere (mobile + desktop + web)
alts.what: One Dart widget codebase for 6 platforms
alts.why: Single UI codebase including desktop with strong performance; best if you will never reuse React/web code
alts.install: winget install Google.Flutter (verify id) or SDK zip

candidates.name: TS/React split-UI monorepo (pick)
candidates.verdict: Shares all logic/types; UI is per-platform (shadcn for web+desktop, RN components for mobile). Best balance of quality and reuse.

candidates.name: Expo-universal + Electron
candidates.verdict: Wins for app-like B2C products where web is secondary; weaker SEO/marketing pages and desktop feel.

candidates.name: Flutter everywhere
candidates.verdict: Wins if one pixel-identical UI matters more than reuse of React web code; Dart is a second language and canvas web is weak for SaaS/SEO.

candidates.name: Capacitor + Electron wrapping the Next/Vite web app
candidates.verdict: Fastest path (one web UI everywhere); mobile feels like a web view and on-device AI/native APIs need plugins.

candidates.name: Tauri 2 for desktop + mobile with web UI
candidates.verdict: One Rust shell for 5 platforms; mobile side is younger than Expo and native AI libraries need Rust.

candidates.name: Kotlin Multiplatform (shared logic) + Compose Multiplatform UI
candidates.verdict: Best for Android-first native teams; no React reuse with web; iOS builds still need a Mac/CI.

candidates.name: .NET MAUI / Avalonia / Uno
candidates.verdict: C# everywhere; MAUI adoption weak, no React reuse, smaller AI-agent ecosystem.

decision: Pick the TS/React monorepo: shared zod schemas, API client, Drizzle schema and domain logic give 60-80% code reuse while each platform keeps a first-class UI. Trade-off: UI components are written twice (web/desktop vs native) - accept it, or switch to Expo-universal when the product is app-first and web is just another client.
details: Typical share: logic/types 100%, state/data hooks (TanStack Query) ~100%, UI 0-30% (design tokens via Tailwind classes on both sides with Uniwind). Python only as a side service for Python-only AI libs (Docling, Presidio).
